subject: Private offer structuring: anchor price versus channel-fee swap
messages:
From: Emma Foster <emma.foster@bluebay-health.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com
Cc: procurement@bluebay-health.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Structuring private offer: anchor price vs channel-fee swap

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We are evaluating Redwood for a multi-region deployment (US + EU) and procurement wants two clean options for a private offer:

1) Anchor-first: Redwood lists at a lower list price and keeps standard channel commission (15%) — BlueBay signs up to a 24-month commit.
2) Channel-fee swap: keep list price close to marketplace list, reduce direct list discount, and apply a one-time channel fee (up-front) to compensate partners.

Key asks from our side:
- Example P&L impact on partner netback for both approaches (we need clarity on how list price changes affect reseller commissions).
- Any constraints on Azure vs GCP SKU parity if we try to harmonize list price across clouds.
- Timeline for closing (we're targeting signature by 8/10).

Can you send a short model and recommended play? Also please include typical language you expect on partner commissions so procurement can review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call this afternoon if helpful.

Emma Foster
Head of Strategic Sourcing
BlueBay Health

Attachment: BlueBay_RFP_outline.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emma Foster <emma.foster@bluebay-health.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Structuring private offer: anchor price vs channel-fee swap

Emma — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary and what I attached: RBW_ChannelModel_v2.xlsx (plays the numbers), and a one-pager runbook.

Short answer: both approaches are workable; tradeoffs below.

Option A — Anchor-first (lower list price)
- Marketplace list price reduced by ~18% to hit BlueBay target unit economics.
- Channel commission remains at Redwood standard 15% on net; partner netback increases slightly because list-price-driven discounts normalize across clouds.
- Pros: Simpler procurement ask (list price + standard commission).
- Cons: lowers reported MSRP which may constrain marketplace comparatives and affects cross-region parity.

Option B — Channel-fee swap (up-front partner fee)
- Keep list price near marketplace level; apply an up-front channel-fee (one-time credit) to partner to equalize netback.
- Channel fee can be amortized over the term for accounting treatment; we suggest a 10% equivalent at signature to approximate the same netback as Option A.
- Pros: preserves list price parity and preserves marketplace comparables.
- Cons: slightly more complex for invoice routing and may require a partner-side invoice/credit path.

Numbers in the spreadsheet include a side-by-side netback for Azure/GCP SKUs and an example of how a $1.2M ARR commit flows through each approach.

Next steps I recommend:
- Review the spreadsheet and mark which option procurement prefers.
- If Channel-fee swap, confirm whether the partner (BlueBay) wants the fee as a vendor invoice or a marketplace pass-through (this affects tax and broker routing).
- We can draft DocuSign-ready terms once you confirm the approach.

Cc'ing Vanessa for channel commission sign-off and Ben for accounting/ops feasibility. Available 3–4pm PT today to talk.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RBW_ChannelModel_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub); Redwood_PrivateOffer_Runbook.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Structuring private offer: anchor price vs channel-fee swap

Sergio/Vanessa — quick internal note from finance/ops review:
- Channel-fee swap is fine but we need to cap the partner invoice path to avoid commingling with marketplace payouts (tax and revenue recognition). Recommend we treat the channel fee as a contra-revenue credit tied to the invoice rather than a reseller commission line.
- If BlueBay insists on vendor invoice, ops will add a 6–8 week lead time for invoicing and settlement.
- Suggest middle-ground: a one-time redemption voucher issued by Redwood to BlueBay (reduces marketplace settlement complexity).

Happy to discuss on the call — if procurement pushes for faster close, Anchor-first is operationally the least friction.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emma Foster <emma.foster@bluebay-health.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Structuring private offer: anchor price vs channel-fee swap

Emma — looping back with a recommended channel-level redline for Option B (channel-fee swap). See attached PDF for the clean language (Vanessa_Proposal_Channels.pdf). Key points:

- Proposal: keep list price at marketplace level; Redwood issues a one-time channel credit equal to 8% of first-year ARR payable to BlueBay within 30 days of activation.
- Commission: BlueBay retains standard 15% commission on net usage; channel credit is separate and non-recurring.
- Invoice path: Redwood issues credit as a vendor-side voucher (reduces complexity for marketplace settlement).
- Territory: credits apply only to US invoices; EU scope requires local tax handling and we will produce an EU addendum if needed.

If that model looks okay to you, we'll prepare a DocuSign package with the private offer and a short SOW. Also attaching a draft SOW for your review: BlueBay_SOW_draft.docx

Can you confirm whether the contract should be Redwood LLC (US) or Redwood EMEA for signing? That determines the legal entity block in the DocuSign.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Channel Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Vanessa_Proposal_Channels.pdf (pdf stub); BlueBay_SOW_draft.docx (docx stub)

From: Emma Foster <emma.foster@bluebay-health.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@bluebay-health.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Structuring private offer: anchor price vs channel-fee swap

Vanessa/Sergio — appreciate the thoroughness. Procurement and our channel team reviewed Option B (your proposed channel credit model) and we're willing to proceed on that basis. Confirmations:

- BlueBay commits to $1.2M ARR year-one (US region) with 24-month term.
- Agree to the one-time channel credit = 8% of first-year ARR payable as Redwood voucher within 30 days of activation.
- Legal entity for signing: Redwood LLC (US).

Please send the revised private offer and DocuSign package and we'll route for sign-off on our side. We prefer the vendor-credit route rather than vendor invoice.

Happy to run a final 15-minute call Monday if you want to walk through the DocuSign.

Best —
Emma Foster
Head of Strategic Sourcing
BlueBay Health

Attachment: BlueBay_Signing_Authorization.pdf (pdf stub); DocuSign request: https://www.docusign.com/au/transaction/ABC-12345
